events.objective: Establish the true symptom onset and blast radius: pinpoint when payment-service error rate and ledger write failures began (exact timestamps), and determine which services beyond payment-service are currently anomalous (check ledger-service and any downstream/upstream services for elevated errors, latency, DB write/connection saturation, queue backlog). Report error signatures/messages for the ledger write failures verbatim, and whether ledger-service itself is healthy or degrading.

Find everything that changed across ALL services in the window 14:30Z–15:10Z on 2026-06-01, not just payment-service: list deployments (especially payment-service v6.0.0 and any ledger-service releases), config changes, and schema/feature-flag changes. Separately, map the service dependency graph around payment-service and ledger-service to identify shared components (DB, queue, config/identity services) and any single point of failure they share.

Search historical incidents for the same error signature (ledger write failures / rejected new ledger entry type / payment failures after deploy) and retrieve precedent: known root cause, whether rollback alone resolved it, and any required follow-up fix (e.g., ledger-service schema or validation change). Also check whether ledger-service has an unreleased or pending configuration that must accompany the new entry type.

args.query: ledger write failures postgres shared database payment timeouts

events.statement: In the window 14:30Z-15:10Z the only deployment across ALL services was payment-service v6.0.0 (id dep-6203) by p.nair at 2026-06-01T14:46:00Z, summary 'New UPI mandate flow', changes ['mandate create/approve endpoints','new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD'], status 'rolled_back' at 2026-06-01T15:12:00Z. This is ~24 min before the 15:10Z report and ~15 min before symptom onset as reported.
No deployment occurred for any ledger component, and no service other than payment-service deployed in the 14:30Z-15:10Z window; deployment count over all services was 1.
Zero config changes were recorded across all services in 14:30Z-15:10Z (count 0, empty list), so no config/flag change explains the onset in that window.
There is no service named 'ledger-service' in the deployment/dependency inventory (query returned not_found); the ledger is represented as 'ledger-db', a postgres node owned by platform.

ledger-db is a SHARED datastore with four writer services: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service all have 'db' edges into ledger-db; each of those services (except payment-service, which is also called by api-gateway) is reached from api-gateway over http. ledger-db is therefore a single shared point of failure coupling payment-service and settlement-service to order-service and portfolio-service.

kafka is a second SHARED component: payment-service and order-service produce to it, while settlement-service and notification-service consume from it, so a kafka problem propagates between the payments and trading/growth paths independently of the v6.0.0 change.

Precedents (leads only, not current-incident evidence): HIST-114 ledger-db disk full / 'no space left on device' write failures; HIST-102 portfolio timeouts during ledger-db primary failover; HIST-105 payment failures from bank-partner-api 5xx; HIST-110 slow orders from ledger-db IOPS throttling. So prior ledger 'write failures' were caused by storage/replication-slot problems, not application code.

events.description: get_deployments with start=end=2026-06-01T16:00:00Z failed with invalid_arguments 'end must be after start', so the post-15:10Z window (including whether the 15:12Z rollback removed the deployment and whether anything else shipped after 15:10Z) was not verified.

No schema-change or feature-flag endpoint was available to me; the only change records returned were deployments (tc-001) and config changes (tc-002, empty). Schema/flag changes are therefore unobserved rather than proven absent.
No metric/trace-level check of ledger-db, kafka or bank-partner-api health (sataturation, connections, lag, 5xx) was performed in this round.

events.answer: Across ALL services only ONE change occurred in 14:30Z–15:10Z: payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203, deployed 14:46:00Z, rolled back 15:12:00Z) introducing the new UPI mandate flow and MANDATE_HOLD ledger entry type; there were zero config/flag changes anywhere. There is no separate "ledger-service" -- the ledger is ledger-db, a SHARED postgres (owner platform) used by payment-service, order-service, portfolio-service and settlement-service, and it is the single shared point of failure behind payment-service and settlement-service; kafka is a second shared component (produced to by payment-service, consumed by settlement-service and notification-service).

events.statement: payment-service error_rate changed from a stable ~0.18–0.28% baseline (14:00–14:55 buckets) to 61.52% in the 15:00:00Z bucket, then held at ~59–64% through 16:55Z (unit: % of requests, HTTP 5xx). The onset is bounded between the 14:55 and 15:00 buckets.

The earliest payment-service ledger write failure is logged at 2026-06-01T15:00:26Z; the dominant (and only) error pattern over 14:00–17:00 is verbatim: 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device (payment e3489438)'. 354 ERROR lines matched, all this single pattern, spanning 15:00:26Z to 16:57:54Z.

ledger-db disk_used_pct rose steadily from 89.39% at 13:00Z, crossed ~99% by 14:50, hit exactly 100.0 at 14:55Z and remained pinned at 100.0% for every 5-minute bucket through 16:55Z. This saturation predates the payment error onset by ~5–10 minutes.

ledger-db itself is failing on writes with verbatim signatures: 'PANIC: could not write to file "pg_wal/xlogtemp.37478": No space left on device' (first at 15:01:01Z, 153 occurrences) and 'could not extend file "base/16402/2619": No space left on device' (first at 15:01:39Z, 139 occurrences). Its top patterns also include WARN 'disk usage 95% on /var/lib/postgresql/data' at 14:15:45Z and 'disk usage 98%' at 14:48:20Z.

Blast radius is not limited to payment-service: order-service error_rate jumped from ~0.18–0.28% to 47.65% in the same 15:00Z bucket, and settlement-service from ~0.13–0.24% to 53.91% in the same 15:00Z bucket; both remain elevated (~47% and ~54%) through 16:55Z. The onset is simultaneous across all three services.

ledger-db exposes WARN about an inactive replication slot retaining WAL ('replication slot 'analytics_cdc' is inactive; retaining 78423 MB of WAL', first seen 14:16:25Z), which is consistent with disk growth, and a late WARN 'clock drift <n>ms detected, resyncing with NTP' first seen 16:23:23Z (clock drift, if real, could affect timestamp precision on ledger-db).

events.description: ledger-db has no 'error_rate' metric; I could not obtain a query-level error/health metric for the database (only connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min exist). connections_active, replication_lag_ms and slow_queries_per_min were not retrieved before the tool budget was exhausted.

Budget exhausted before I could query api-gateway and auth-service error_rate and settlement-service consumer_lag (queue backlog), and before checking other upstream/downstream services (notification-service, exchange-gateway, kafka).

The 15:00:00Z bucket (5-min) is the first anomalous bucket for all three services, so onset cannot be pin-pointed finer than 14:55–15:00 from metrics; the log first-error at 15:00:26Z gives the tightest lower bound for payment-service.

events.answer: Payment-service error rate jumped from a ~0.2% baseline to ~60% starting in the 15:00–15:05 bucket on 2026-06-01, with the first ledger write failure logged at 15:00:26Z — i.e. the symptom onset precedes the 15:10 report and is driven by ledger-db disk saturation, not only by the v6.0.0 release. ledger-db (the "ledger-service") is critically degrading: disk_used_pct reached 100% at ~14:55–15:00 and stayed there, and it is emitting "No space left on device" PANIC/extend-file errors. Blast radius extends beyond payment-service: order-service (~48%) and settlement-service (~55%) error rates also jumped in the same 15:00 bucket.

rejected new ledger entry type schema validation after deploy payment failures
replication slot WAL retained disk growth ledger-db resolution dropped slot
rollback did not resolve payment failures required follow-up fix capacity

events.statement: Precedent HIST-114 (2025-04-18, 'ledger-db disk full from retained WAL') is the closest known match to the current signature: services ['ledger-db'], symptoms ['no space left on device','write failures'], root_cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled', category resource_exhaustion, resolution 'Dropped slot; added slot-lag alert'. It matched both the write-failure query (match_score 10) and the retained-WAL query (match_score 7).

The HIST-114 precedent was resolved by two steps beyond stopping the writer: 'Dropped slot; added slot-lag alert' — i.e. clearing the retained WAL on the storage layer plus adding monitoring, not by rolling back an application release. The incident record lists no application-code change as cause or fix.

No historical incident in the retrieved precedents matches 'rejected new ledger entry type' / ledger schema-validation-after-deploy: the entry-type/schema query returned HIST-109 (JWT library clock-skew, match 3), HIST-105 (bank partner 5xx, 2), HIST-108 (JWT key rotation, 2), HIST-111 (unindexed report query, 2), HIST-114 (disk full, 2), HIST-101 (bcrypt cost, 1) — none describe a rejected new ledger entry type or a ledger-service schema/validation change.

Precedent ledger 'write failures' in the corpus have non-application root causes: HIST-114 = inactive replication slot retaining WAL (resource_exhaustion); HIST-102 = unplanned ledger-db primary failover / refused connections (infrastructure_failure); HIST-110 = ledger-db IOPS throttling / burst credits exhausted (infrastructure_failure); HIST-111 = unindexed reporting query (bad_deployment, but a reporting job, not a ledger write path). No precedent attributes ledger write failures to a rejected new entry type from a payment-service release.

No unreleased or pending ledger-db configuration change was found: config-change queries returned count 0 for both all-services (2026-06-01T00:00–16:59Z) and ledger-db scope (2026-05-01T00:00–2026-06-01T14:30Z), and the ledger-db deployment query (2026-05-01–2026-06-01T15:15Z) returned count 0 with an empty deployments list. So nothing in the change/config inventory supplies a pending schema or flag that must accompany the MANDATE_HOLD entry type.

Precedent for whether rollback alone suffices is only partial and points the other way: the code-regression precedents were resolved by rollback (HIST-109 'Rolled back; pinned skew config', HIST-101 'Rolled back v6.4.0'), whereas the ledger-db write-failure precedent HIST-114 required dropping the slot and adding an alert. The corpus contains no incident where a payment-service release caused ledger write failures and rollback alone resolved it.

events.description: Historical incident records expose only title/services/symptoms/root_cause/resolution; there is no per-incident timeline, no verbatim error text, and no post-incident verification of whether the writer rollback alone restored writes before the storage fix. The sweep for a 'rejected new ledger entry type / schema-validation-after-deploy' precedent returned only loosely related incidents (max match_score 3), so there is no confirmed precedent for that specific signature.

Deployment and config-change inventories return only itemized change events (deployments + config changes). They contain no ledger-db setting/parameter list (e.g. DB config keys such as replication slot settings, disk/autovacuum/WAL retention parameters) and no notion of an 'unreleased' or 'pending' config value, so a pending ledger config that must accompany MANDATE_HOLD could not be inspected directly.

events.answer: Precedent search found one strong, on-signature match: HIST-114 (2025-04-18, ledger-db) with the same symptoms ('no space left on device', 'write failures'), root cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled' (resource_exhaustion), and resolution 'Dropped slot; added slot-lag alert' — i.e. prior ledger write failures were a storage/replication-slot problem fixed at the ledger-db layer, not by rolling back application code; there is NO precedent for a rejected new ledger entry type or a ledger-service schema/validation change (the schema/entry-type query returned only unrelated incidents, max match_score 3). Consistently, no ledger-db deployment or config change exists from 2026-05-01 to the incident (config count 0 for all-services and ledger-db; deployments count 0), so nothing in the change inventory is a pending config that must accompany the new MANDATE_HOLD entry type. Precedent therefore suggests rollback of payment-service v6.0.0 alone is unlikely to clear the write failures (the ledger-db storage condition, matching the team's disk-saturation evidence, would persist), and a follow-up fix analogous to HIST-114 (clear/drop the inactive replication slot retaining WAL, add slot-lag alerting) is indicated — though the HIST-114 record itself does not prove rollback-alone insufficiency.

events.title: ledger-db disk exhaustion from retained WAL (shared infra) — payment v6.0.0 is a coincidental pairing
payment-service v6.0.0 mandate flow regression writes a bad MANDATE_HOLD payload ledger-db cannot accept
Independent shared-dependency failure (kafka or bank-partner-api) as the common trigger
Shared ledger-db failure that is configuration/schema-triggered — a pending ledger config or migration that must accompany MANDATE_HOLD

events.summary: H1 (ledger-db disk exhaustion as the shared origin, payment v6.0.0 as coincidental amplifier) is adequately supported: disk_used_pct is VERIFIED at 100.0% from 14:55Z and pinned through 16:55Z (F10), ledger-db itself PANICs with verbatim "No space left on device" on pg_wal/xlogtemp and base/* (F11), payment's only error pattern is the same storage error (F9), and order-service/settlement-service — which never received v6.0.0 and do not use the mandate flow — spike in the same 15:00Z bucket (F12, F5). Cause precedes onset (disk full 14:55Z vs first write error 15:00:26Z). H2/H4 are contradicted on mechanism (validation vs storage error), scope (non-payment writers fail) and inventory (F3/F18: zero config/deploy changes); H3 is contradicted by the disk-full error signature and rests on an unrun check. Crucially, the decisive discriminator against H2 is already in-hand: all three services stay elevated (61/48/54%) through 16:55Z while disk stays at 100% and after the 15:12Z rollback (F8, F12, F10) — no recovery on rollback. Residual weakness: the specific claim that the analytics_cdc inactive slot's retained WAL is what filled the disk is inference-only (F13 is VERIFIED/inference, no WAL-size or slot-size metric, no post-clear recovery observation), and ledger-db connection/replication-lag saturation was never measured. Those affect the *mechanism detail*, not the *origin* (ledger-db storage layer) or the fix direction, so they lower confidence rather than block.

tasks.objective: Establish the true symptom onset and blast radius: pinpoint when payment-service error rate and ledger write failures began (exact timestamps), and determine which services beyond payment-service are currently anomalous (check ledger-service and any downstream/upstream services for elevated errors, latency, DB write/connection saturation, queue backlog). Report error signatures/messages for the ledger write failures verbatim, and whether ledger-service itself is healthy or degrading.
tasks.answer: Payment-service error rate jumped from a ~0.2% baseline to ~60% starting in the 15:00–15:05 bucket on 2026-06-01, with the first ledger write failure logged at 15:00:26Z — i.e. the symptom onset precedes the 15:10 report and is driven by ledger-db disk saturation, not only by the v6.0.0 release. ledger-db (the "ledger-service") is critically degrading: disk_used_pct reached 100% at ~14:55–15:00 and stayed there, and it is emitting "No space left on device" PANIC/extend-file errors. Blast radius extends beyond payment-service: order-service (~48%) and settlement-service (~55%) error rates also jumped in the same 15:00 bucket.

tasks.objective: Find everything that changed across ALL services in the window 14:30Z–15:10Z on 2026-06-01, not just payment-service: list deployments (especially payment-service v6.0.0 and any ledger-service releases), config changes, and schema/feature-flag changes. Separately, map the service dependency graph around payment-service and ledger-service to identify shared components (DB, queue, config/identity services) and any single point of failure they share.
tasks.answer: Across ALL services only ONE change occurred in 14:30Z–15:10Z: payment-service v6.0.0 (dep-6203, deployed 14:46:00Z, rolled back 15:12:00Z) introducing the new UPI mandate flow and MANDATE_HOLD ledger entry type; there were zero config/flag changes anywhere. There is no separate "ledger-service" -- the ledger is ledger-db, a SHARED postgres (owner platform) used by payment-service, order-service, portfolio-service and settlement-service, and it is the single shared point of failure behind payment-service and settlement-service; kafka is a second shared component (produced to by payment-service, consumed by settlement-service and notification-service).

tasks.objective: Search historical incidents for the same error signature (ledger write failures / rejected new ledger entry type / payment failures after deploy) and retrieve precedent: known root cause, whether rollback alone resolved it, and any required follow-up fix (e.g., ledger-service schema or validation change). Also check whether ledger-service has an unreleased or pending configuration that must accompany the new entry type.
tasks.answer: Precedent search found one strong, on-signature match: HIST-114 (2025-04-18, ledger-db) with the same symptoms ('no space left on device', 'write failures'), root cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled' (resource_exhaustion), and resolution 'Dropped slot; added slot-lag alert' — i.e. prior ledger write failures were a storage/replication-slot problem fixed at the ledger-db layer, not by rolling back application code; there is NO precedent for a rejected new ledger entry type or a ledger-service schema/validation change (the schema/entry-type query returned only unrelated incidents, max match_score 3). Consistently, no ledger-db deployment or config change exists from 2026-05-01 to the incident (config count 0 for all-services and ledger-db; deployments count 0), so nothing in the change inventory is a pending config that must accompany the new MANDATE_HOLD entry type. Precedent therefore suggests rollback of payment-service v6.0.0 alone is unlikely to clear the write failures (the ledger-db storage condition, matching the team's disk-saturation evidence, would persist), and a follow-up fix analogous to HIST-114 (clear/drop the inactive replication slot retaining WAL, add slot-lag alerting) is indicated — though the HIST-114 record itself does not prove rollback-alone insufficiency.

critiques.summary: H1 (ledger-db disk exhaustion as the shared origin, payment v6.0.0 as coincidental amplifier) is adequately supported: disk_used_pct is VERIFIED at 100.0% from 14:55Z and pinned through 16:55Z (F10), ledger-db itself PANICs with verbatim "No space left on device" on pg_wal/xlogtemp and base/* (F11), payment's only error pattern is the same storage error (F9), and order-service/settlement-service — which never received v6.0.0 and do not use the mandate flow — spike in the same 15:00Z bucket (F12, F5). Cause precedes onset (disk full 14:55Z vs first write error 15:00:26Z). H2/H4 are contradicted on mechanism (validation vs storage error), scope (non-payment writers fail) and inventory (F3/F18: zero config/deploy changes); H3 is contradicted by the disk-full error signature and rests on an unrun check. Crucially, the decisive discriminator against H2 is already in-hand: all three services stay elevated (61/48/54%) through 16:55Z while disk stays at 100% and after the 15:12Z rollback (F8, F12, F10) — no recovery on rollback. Residual weakness: the specific claim that the analytics_cdc inactive slot's retained WAL is what filled the disk is inference-only (F13 is VERIFIED/inference, no WAL-size or slot-size metric, no post-clear recovery observation), and ledger-db connection/replication-lag saturation was never measured. Those affect the *mechanism detail*, not the *origin* (ledger-db storage layer) or the fix direction, so they lower confidence rather than block.

challenges.issue: The first causal hop — that the inactive 'analytics_cdc' replication slot's retained WAL (78 GB) is what filled the disk — is inference-only. No metric shows WAL/slot size growth or that dropping the slot reduces disk usage; F13 is VERIFIED/inference ('consistent with'). An alternative unmeasured bloat/table-growth mechanism could explain the same 100% disk. This changes the specific storage mechanism, not the origin or fix direction, but caps confidence below the stated 0.72+.

ledger-db connection saturation, replication_lag_ms and slow_queries were never retrieved (GAPS), and ledger-db has no error_rate metric, so the write-saturation picture rests on disk_used_pct plus log signatures only.
kafka/bank-partner-api health was explicitly never checked; the rejection rests on the disk-full error signature being inconsistent with those faults, not on a contradicted measurement.

Rejection asserts rollback did not clear the symptom, but the post-15:12Z recovery check is not tied to a single explicit finding — it is inferred from F8/F12 persistence vs F10 disk pinning. The evidence is present (services remain elevated after the 15:12Z rollback while disk stays 100%), so this is confirmatory, not blocking.

evidence_requests.question: For ledger-db, plot disk_used_pct alongside WAL/slot size (or any available retention/disk-growth metric) around 14:16Z-15:00Z, and confirm whether the disk remained at 100% and payment/order/settlement error_rate remained elevated (~60/48/54%) after the payment-service v6.0.0 rollback at 15:12Z through 16:55Z. This is confirmation that the origin is the persistent ledger-db storage condition rather than the caller-side release.
evidence_requests.rationale: Tightens the decisive discriminator vs H2 and verifies the inferred slot->disk-growth hop; low-cost, data already partially in findings.
